records.value: `Blueprint.register` can nest a child, with parent prefixes on endpoint names and URLs. Parent callbacks apply to descendants. A parent error handler is tried only if the child cannot handle the exception.
records.initial_value: `Blueprint.__init__` creates a reusable registration recipe, not an independent application.

records.value: `Blueprint.add_url_rule` once allowed dotted view names to misidentify the active blueprint and skip its authentication callback.
`Request.blueprint` is derived from the endpoint identity; dots inside a view name previously changed that identity.
`Blueprint.register` applies operations recorded earlier to the application receiving that component.
`Flask.register_blueprint` supports mounting a component more than once; its implementation must support repeated registration.
`Flask.__init__` supports separate application instances with different configurations in one process.
`Flask.app_context` supplies the active application without requiring a request, supporting multiple applications in one process.
`Flask.create_url_adapter` must preserve opt-in subdomain matching; setting the server name alone stopped enabling it.
`RequestContext.push` must reuse an already opened session so streaming observes changes made by the view.
`stream_with_context` keeps request data available while a response generator runs after the view has returned.
Components share their owning application configuration; independent applications are combined at the gateway layer instead.
A component name prefixes endpoint identities. Changing that name does not itself change the mounted URL.
A registered component cannot be unregistered independently; rebuilding the application is required.
Application templates take precedence over component templates, allowing the application to override reusable component presentation.
Factories allow tests to create independently configured application instances instead of reusing one global instance.
Reusable extension objects keep application-specific state outside the shared extension object so several applications can use one extension.
Reusable components cannot depend on one application object at import time; request-time access uses the active application.
Shell and command-line work may need an application context even when no HTTP request exists.
Context-local resources are acquired lazily and released by context teardown rather than stored as process-wide shared state.
Context-local application and request state is isolated between threads rather than shared as ordinary globals.
Pushing a test request context does not run the entire request dispatch lifecycle automatically.
`Flask.do_teardown_request` runs when a request context is removed, including failure paths; cleanup cannot assume successful dispatch.
The view returns before its response generator is consumed, so request-bound work in the generator needs preserved context.
Streaming observes the existing session, but changing a cookie-backed session after response headers are sent cannot update those headers.
`FlaskGroup` is the application-aware parent of management commands. Custom Click drivers are supported, but application commands must run beneath a FlaskGroup so they know which application to use.

`AppGroup.command` wraps callbacks in an application context by default. Commands attached later with Click add_command do not receive that wrapper automatically; with_appcontext=False explicitly opts out.
`Flask.make_shell_context` supplies shell locals after the correct application context has been established. The default shell exposes the application and g.
FLASK_APP can identify a module or a filename. A colon suffix chooses an application object whose name differs from app.
Flask uses Click so reusable applications can ship a custom management driver integrated into a larger command-line application.
A custom FlaskGroup receives an application factory and asks it to create the application when Click needs to operate on it. This lets the driver control application construction.
Click runs parameter callbacks after parsing and value conversion. Eager parameters run before ordinary parameters. This applies to Flask CLI callbacks such as `_validate_key`.
